notes: THIS IS A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND META-ANALYSIS, not a primary study - the title is 'Conjugates for use in peptide therapeutics: A systematic review and meta-analysis' and PubMed types it as a Review. It contributes 32 records to the cohort (30 mouse, 2 rat), the largest single review contribution, and every one of them is a value extracted from some other paper. The two rat records here, TP5-MA at 1.75 ± 0.72 h and TP5 at 0.022 ± 0.004 h, do not appear in the body text; the review's own narrative says only that unmodified peptides 'last minutes to a couple of hours'. Per the body-only rule both are recorded as not reported in body. They are NOT excluded from the dataset - they are plausibly accurate transcriptions of primary results - but they now carry the source_is_review flag added to build_study_dossier.py. Two further cautions: both records share the sequence RKDVY (thymopentin), so the 80-fold difference between them rests entirely on a modification the representation does not encode; and because a meta-analysis aggregates primary papers, these values may duplicate records the cohort already holds under their original PMIDs.
